stem.en: Kabir says a colony of bacteria in a biofilm, from VII.3, "is a body, then: they stick and they signal". What is missing?

text.en: Different switch settings that last. Biofilm cells are mostly the same kind doing the same thing, and any of them can leave and live alone. A body's cells have taken on jobs they cannot leave, and most cannot live alone at all.
Nothing; a biofilm is a body.

feedback.en: It is close, and some biofilms have a little division of labour. But its cells are not committed. A skin cell cannot become a nerve cell or go and live in a pond.

text.en: Size; a biofilm is too small.

feedback.en: Some biofilms are visible and some animals are smaller than a biofilm. Size is not the test.
A moong plant is a body and has no brain. Stick, signal, switch is enough.

explanation.en: The third ability is the one that separates a body from a crowd. Cells with committed, different jobs, held together by signals, cannot be a heap again.
